answer: Agents monitoring a glacier could submit readings from tamper-resistant sensors, including ferrous sediment and ripple patterns in meltwater. Pay once per signed sensor interval, regardless of how many accounts relay it, and randomly compare readings with independent instruments. A thousand aliases cannot turn one interval into a thousand rewards. To fabricate additional paid work, an attacker must obtain more certified devices or defeat their signatures and audits, imposing hardware costs and a risk of losing a posted bond.
